scope: Executable or predictive world models learned from interaction, with validation, planning, or repair; direct web work and explicitly labeled adjacent work are distinguished.
sources_policy: Official papers (arXiv/proceedings), author project pages, and author repositories only.

papers.title: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
papers.problem: Clone target websites into safe synthetic full-stack environments; generate tasks with executable validators to train self-evolving web agents.
papers.input_access: Coding agent uses screenshots/site descriptions to build synthetic front end, back end and database; learner observes browser interface and acts in clones; validator has privileged Python SDK/database access.
papers.representation: Executable synthetic website plus task-specific Python validator; agent policy is fine-tuned trajectories, not an executable learned transition model.
papers.learning: Offline rejection-based supervised fine-tuning from successful agent trajectories, followed by iterative self-evolving task/trajectory generation; not online induction of a website dynamics program.
papers.inference_use: Train web-agent policy and evaluate task outcomes in recreated sites; tasks receive deterministic programmatic reward.
papers.correction: Environment construction uses coding-agent debugging; task validators can be rerun. No explicit learned rulebook/code-model correction loop.
papers.evaluation: WebArena-Lite five sites, Mind2Web-Online (220 usable tasks), site-specific cloned WebArena settings; 149 constructed sites, 7,400 tasks.
measured_results: Paper Table 3: 30 independent human-evaluation instances, double annotated (60 annotation judgments); task executability 90%, judge correctness 76%, mean functional correctness 90.3%, visual rating 4.7/5, mean Cohen kappa 0.61.

Paper Table 4 WebArena-Lite total: Qwen3-4B 7.88% to +VERIENV 13.94% (+6.06 percentage points); LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct 3.03% to 12.73% (table delta +9.70). Body text says +9.09 for the latter, an internal inconsistency; report table arithmetic and flag discrepancy.
Paper Table 1: 149 websites, average 49.5 tasks/site, total 7,400 tasks.
papers.code_and_weights: Author repository public as checked 2026-10-20. Training uses GPT-5.2/Cursor cloning and rejection fine-tuning on Qwen3-4B or LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct; Luna inference adaptation is not reproduction of the original training results.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Website cloning and verifiable reward are relevant infrastructure; this is not online code world-model learning. The current self-built miniweb is not GitLab or WebArena, and WebArena is not a dependency.

papers.title: WorldCoder, a Model-Based LLM Agent: Building World Models by Writing Code and Interacting with the Environment
papers.problem: Learn a transferable symbolic dynamics model from few environment interactions and use it for goal-directed planning.
papers.input_access: Structured object states and action/reward/termination transitions; natural-language goal. Assumes deterministic fixed dynamics across goals.
papers.representation: Python transition function and separate goal-conditioned reward/termination function over object-oriented MDP state.
papers.learning: Online interaction buffer; GPT-4 program synthesis/refinement against replay constraints plus optimistic reachability constraint.
papers.inference_use: Depth-limited value iteration or MCTS; after model learning, new goals mainly require reward-function extension.
papers.correction: Counterexample-guided LLM code refinement; can refine old model for new dynamics.
papers.evaluation: Sokoban, MiniGrid, ALFWorld; not browser environments.
measured_results: Sokoban model built over first 50 actions; reported ReAct success on basic levels 15% +/- 8%.
Paper Figure 3 reports deep RL needs >1 million steps to learn 2-box Sokoban; apples-to-apples scope is the paper's particular basic level setup.
After front-loading about 400k LLM tokens (~$15 in paper setup), actions can be issued without further LLM queries.
papers.code_and_weights: Author code is public; README notes legacy NumPy/Gymnasium/MiniGrid compatibility. Original experiments use GPT-4, so same-model Luna port is not a results reproduction.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Structured states and deterministic MDP assumptions differ from asynchronous, partially observed web pages and backend side effects.

papers.title: Generating Code World Models with Large Language Models Guided by Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.problem: Improve success and search efficiency for LLM-generated Python environment/world models.
papers.input_access: Replayable transitions and environment/task descriptions; structured state/action interfaces.
papers.representation: Python Environment.step(s,a) returning next state, reward and done.
papers.learning: Mostly offline/inference-time program generation and refinement; GIF-MCTS explores candidates and requests feedback from execution/replay tests.
papers.inference_use: Run learned code as simulator for planning/model-based RL; program prediction avoids calling an LLM for each simulated step.
papers.correction: Generate/Improve/Fix candidate program edits guided by MCTS and test feedback.
papers.evaluation: APPS, Code World Models Benchmark, Gym-style environments; no web benchmark.
measured_results: Paper Table 1, APPS competition split strict accuracy, Llama 3 70B, pass@20: GIF-MCTS 28.3% +/- 1.4; reimplemented WorldCoder 25.1% +/- 1.4; reimplemented zero-shot CoT 23.2% +/- 1.3.
Strict accuracy means all unit tests for a problem pass; it is not next-state prediction accuracy or web task success.

Paper Table 2 (arXiv v2), CWMB 18 environments, Llama 3 70B, 50 calls, 3 seeds: discrete accuracy/normalized return 0.84 +/- 0.03 / 0.76 +/- 0.03; continuous 0.35 +/- 0.03 / 0.22 +/- 0.01. Reimplemented WorldCoder: discrete 0.79 +/- 0.04 / 0.60 +/- 0.04; continuous 0.32 +/- 0.03 / 0.19 +/- 0.01. Planning return is also averaged over 10 episodes; normalization sets random-policy return to zero and true-model same-planner return to one.
papers.code_and_weights: Author code and replay buffers are public; README documents model and LLM call budget requirements. Original result is not a Luna replication.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Testing/program synthesis framework is relevant; benchmark domains and state representations are not browser tasks.

papers.title: Web Agents with World Models: Learning and Leveraging Environment Dynamics in Web Navigation
papers.problem: Predict web action outcomes to improve action selection and avoid costly mistakes.
papers.input_access: Instruction, current web observation/accessibility structure, and candidate action; training transitions drawn from WebArena/Mind2Web trajectories.
papers.representation: Fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct predicts free-form natural-language transition-focused differences; value model ranks candidates.
papers.learning: Offline supervised model fine-tuning on web trajectory differences; frozen policy at inference.
papers.inference_use: Sample candidate actions, predict each outcome, use value model to select one; no policy fine-tuning required for deployment.
papers.correction: Can use simulated outcomes for action self-refinement; world model itself is not an explicit online rule repair system.
papers.evaluation: WebArena (five domains including GitLab) and Mind2Web; separate ablations/preliminary analyses.
measured_results: Paper Table 1, WebArena, GPT-4o, max actions=5: 12.8% without action selection vs 16.6% with WMA selection (+29.7% relative). GPT-4o-mini: 9.4% vs 13.5% (+43.6% relative).
Paper Table 2, GPT-4o-mini GitLab: Vanilla CoT 3.1%, WMA 8.7%; this is the original WebArena GitLab split, not the current self-built miniweb.
Paper error analysis uses 100 samples and GPT-4o judging; 42% of categorized prediction errors are counterfactual imagined elements.
papers.code_and_weights: Official repo and Llama adapters/datasets are public. Original training requires Llama fine-tuning; prompting Luna is only inference adaptation.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Strong same-domain baseline for lookahead, but language predictions are not executable rules and model correction is not the paper's contribution.

papers.title: PoE-World: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts
papers.problem: Learn stochastic non-grid world dynamics compositionally from sparse observations rather than synthesizing one monolithic program.
papers.input_access: Object-centric Atari frame descriptions/actions and brief demonstrations; not web DOM or backend state.
papers.representation: Exponentially weighted product of many LLM-synthesized programmatic experts, each encoding causal laws.
papers.learning: Program synthesis/refinement from few observations; replay/prediction scoring evaluates candidates.
papers.inference_use: Hierarchical lookahead planner or simulator for policy pretraining and subsequent environment fine-tuning.
papers.correction: Expert acquisition and refinement from observed transitions; no web-specific ongoing correction mechanism.
papers.evaluation: Atari Pong, Pong-Alt, Montezuma's Revenge and MR-Alt.
measured_results: Paper Table 1: PoE-World + Planner Pong -12.33 +/- 0.88, Pong-Alt -13.67 +/- 0.67, MR 100 +/- 0, MR-Alt 100 +/- 0.
For these model-based rows, brief demonstrations initialize models, followed by at most 3k training steps; scores differ by game and are not comparable with web task success.
PPO pretraining in the model reaches better-than-random performance after 200k real training steps versus 1M for vanilla PPO, per paper text.
papers.code_and_weights: Author project/code available; experiments use OpenAI LLM calls and substantial planner compute, not a frozen Luna-only run.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Useful modular-rule alternative; stochastic visual game dynamics differ from web business state.

papers.title: Is Your LLM Secretly a World Model of the Internet? Model-Based Planning for Web Agents
papers.problem: Use pretrained LLM simulation to improve inference-time web planning without relying on expensive live tree search.
papers.input_access: Web observation, candidate action, and task; experiments include screenshots and accessibility/DOM-style inputs.
papers.representation: LLM-generated textual hypothetical next observation and progress score; not a persistent executable site model.
papers.learning: Primarily inference-time prompting; author also releases Dreamer-7B and web world-model training resources.
papers.inference_use: Generate candidate actions, simulate outcomes, score, execute best action; generally single-step lookahead.
papers.correction: No explicit counterexample-based model repair; reactive observation can ground later turns.
measured_results: Paper Table 1: GPT-4o WebDreamer success rates 23.6% VisualWebArena, 37.0% Online-Mind2Web, 25.0% Mind2Web-Live; reactive baseline 17.6%, 26.0%, 20.2%, respectively.
Table 2 reports WebDreamer wall time 183.6–233.7 seconds versus reactive 68.3–87.7 seconds across three VWA domains; successful lookahead has compute cost.
papers.code_and_weights: Author repository and Dreamer-7B/HF resources public; versioned repo lists model/data release. Original GPT-4o setting is distinct from a Luna prompt adaptation.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Same-domain non-code baseline; susceptible to plausible but false imagined page content.

papers.title: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Co-evolving World Model
papers.problem: Reduce stagnation in self-improving web agents by co-evolving a world model with the policy.
papers.input_access: Current page/accessibility tree and attempted browser action from web trajectories.
papers.representation: World-model LLM predicts next observation; acts as a virtual web server and an inference-time lookahead simulator.
papers.learning: Co-evolving model/policy and self-sampled trajectory training; requires model fine-tuning.
papers.inference_use: Generate synthetic training trajectories and simulate candidate action outcomes at test time.
papers.correction: World-model weights evolve through training; no explicit inspectable rulebook or rule/code diagnosis.
papers.evaluation: Text WebVoyager (473-query test split), filtered Mind2Web-Live (53-query test split), and other real-web tasks including GAIA-Web.
measured_results: Paper Table 1 denominators: WebVoyager 473 queries and Mind2Web-Live-filtered 53 queries. Llama-3.3-70B initial self-improve scores are 32.98%/18.86% (WV/M2W-Live); WebEvolver 42.49%/22.64%; WebEvolver + depth-2 WMLA 51.37%/24.53%. Two time-window runs are averaged and trajectories are GPT-4o-evaluated.

Paper Table 2 intrinsic judge for world-model iteration 2 at lookahead depth 1: structural correctness/similarity/overall assessment 75.96/63.56/72.86%; depths greater than 2 fall below 50% on these measures.
Abstract claims about 10% improvement are not a universal percentage-point gain; exact interpretation is comparison-specific.
papers.code_and_weights: Author code is public; full method depends on learned world model and agent training resources, so Luna prompting is not a reproduction.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Relevant continual web training concept, but much less transparent rule correction than an executable model.

papers.title: PatchWorld: Gradient-Free Optimization of Executable World Models for Agent Environments
papers.problem: Induce interpretable persistent belief-state programs from sparse offline trajectories and repair them using execution-grounded counterexamples.
papers.input_access: Offline text observation/action/next-observation trajectories only; no live exploration during induction.
papers.representation: Python BaseWorldModel with parser, explicit belief, belief correction, transition prediction and observation readout.
papers.learning: Offline candidate synthesis plus replay validation and gradient-free local repair; held-out test split reserved for evaluation.
papers.inference_use: One-step lookahead/action reranking; agent still uses LLM to propose/select candidate actions in the paper's live protocol.
papers.correction: Typed execution validator exposes replay errors; LLM synthesizes/repairs model and accepts only replay improvements.
papers.evaluation: Seven AgentGym text environments: AlfWorld, BabyAI, Maze, SciWorld, TextCraft, WebShop, Wordle.
measured_results: Abstract: PatchWorld-Simple 76.4% macro success in live one-step lookahead across seven environments.
Paper Table 2: PatchWorld-Residual with Qwen3-Coder-480B reaches 0.69 Token-F1 / 0.50 BLEU-4 on held-out next-observation prediction; up to 0.70 Token-F1 with Mimo-v2.5 or DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
Paper Table 3 rollout Token-F1 at horizons 1/2/3/5: LLM-Direct .64/.63/.60/.59; WorldCoder .63/.60/.58/.57; PoE-World .63/.57/.53/.51; PatchWorld-Simple .56/.50/.43/.40.
Paper reports about 17–28 LLM calls and 300k–503k tokens per environment for offline induction; zero world-model LLM calls during prediction.
papers.code_and_weights: Author code public, MIT; trajectory dataset separately on Hugging Face. LLM backbones include Qwen3-Coder-480B, Mimo-v2.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash. No LLM calls in the model prediction module does not mean the complete agent has no LLM.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Closest executable correction baseline, but offline trajectories and AgentGym are not online interaction with the current self-built miniweb; requires a local adaptation and honest label.

papers.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks
papers.problem: Maintain and revise explicit environment hypotheses when observations are sparse and several models fit past evidence.
papers.input_access: Interactive action interface and observation/trajectory history; no source inspection in ARC-AGI-3 setup.
papers.representation: Markdown rulebook for objects, action semantics, dynamics, goals and unresolved alternatives; Python executable for internal states, prediction, rendering and goals.
papers.learning: Online continual reflection from interaction history with frozen Claude Opus 5; persistent rulebook/program workspace.
papers.inference_use: Replay-validated model reconstructs state, then planner searches model dynamics and executes actions.
papers.correction: LLM chooses retain, revise rulebook or repair code; compiler emits implementation; exact replay verifier gates use.
papers.evaluation: 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games and Atari Pong case study, not web.
measured_results: Paper Table 1: RHAE 100 on all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games; 7,518 actions, reported as 44% of human action count.
Pong: 21:0 in three evaluated episodes with different openings, no LLM calls during execution.
Table 3 rulebook ablation samples only one game per difficulty band: with rulebook uses 75/341/201 actions on ft09/ka59/cn04 vs without 79/382/216.
papers.code_and_weights: Paper uses Claude Opus 5 extra-high and coding-agent harness; no author repository or downloadable weights found in checked official materials. Memento PDF is the parent-directory 2610.11794v1.pdf; VeriEnv paper is the local chae26a.pdf.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Directly reviewed from parent-directory local PDF and arXiv HTML. Exact historical replay does not establish unseen-state prediction; ARC actions and benchmark scoring differ from business web tasks.

papers.title: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
papers.problem: Train a scalable simulator of the open web from large-scale interactions for agent data and inference-time search.
papers.input_access: More than one million open-web interaction trajectories; simulator supports reasoning, multi-format observations and 30+ step rollouts.
papers.representation: Learned web simulator/world model, not an inspectable Python site transition model.
papers.inference_use: Generate synthetic agent trajectories and support inference-time search.
papers.correction: No explicit local rulebook/code repair loop described in abstract/checked source.
papers.evaluation: WebWorld-Bench intrinsic simulator metrics and extrinsic WebArena agent training.
measured_results: Paper Table 5: Qwen3-14B WebArena success 15.1% before and 24.3% after training on 8,000 synthesized trajectories (+9.2 percentage points); table does not state denominator.
Paper Table 6: MiniWoB greedy 64.3%; WebWorld with GPT-5 pairwise scoring and BoN(3) 67.5%. Table denominator not reported here; distinct benchmark/protocol.
papers.code_and_weights: Author repository public; README lists WebWorld-32B and open model/data resources.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Direct web simulation background but does not test active local-site rule induction or executable rule correction.

papers.title: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
papers.problem: Predict action-conditioned next GUI appearance with controllable structure and visual fidelity.
papers.input_access: Android screenshot, action and goal; AndroidWorld navigation evaluation comprises 116 tasks.
papers.representation: Vision-language model generates renderable HTML for the next screenshot.
papers.learning: SFT followed by render-aware reinforcement learning; visual feedback revises synthesized data.
papers.inference_use: Render candidate next states to support propose-simulate-select GUI navigation.
papers.correction: Visual feedback loop refines data/code generation; no persistent web business rule update demonstrated.
papers.evaluation: Next UI prediction and AndroidWorld navigation.
measured_results: Paper Figure 6: AndroidWorld, Gemini-2.5-Flash baseline 41.4% and Code2World-assisted 50.9% (+9.5 percentage points); 116-task benchmark. This is Android navigation, not web success.
Paper Table 2 AndroidControl-High: Mobile-Agent-v3-7B success 67.20%?68.41%; Qwen2.5-VL-7B 65.16%?66.47% with Code2World. Separate benchmark and protocol.
papers.code_and_weights: Author repository, data, and model are linked from project materials; full use requires released model resources and is not a Luna reproduction.
papers.limits_for_local_study: GUI rendering and next screenshot fidelity are distinct from semantic business state transition and multi-step rule repair.

papers.title: Agent2World: Learning to Generate Symbolic World Models via Adaptive Multi-Agent Feedback
papers.problem: Improve generation of PDDL and executable symbolic world models using adaptive feedback, and create SFT data.
papers.input_access: World-model specifications, web-researched knowledge and generated models tested in unit tests/simulation; not browser interaction.
papers.representation: Generated PDDL domain or executable simulator code.
papers.learning: Inference-time researcher/developer/tester agents; testing trajectories also used to fine-tune a model.
papers.inference_use: Generate validated symbolic world models for downstream planning.
papers.correction: Adaptive test team returns behavior-level feedback to model developer.
papers.evaluation: Three general world-model generation benchmarks spanning PDDL and executable code; no web agent benchmark.
measured_results: Paper Table 1 Text2World: GPT-4.1-mini Agent2World Multi executability 93.1%.
Paper Table 2 CWMB overall accuracy/normalized return: Agent2World 0.5441/0.4811 vs Direct Generation 0.4466/0.2620.
Paper Table 3 ByteSized32 runnable-game metric: 0.8958. These are world-model generation benchmarks, not web interaction.
papers.code_and_weights: Author repository public with benchmark scripts. Full SFT uses Llama-3.1-8B and 8?A100 resources; repository presence does not mean Luna can run the trained method.
papers.limits_for_local_study: Useful model tester feedback architecture; differs from a persistent site model learned online by one agent.

local_experiment_guidance.environment: Self-built, resettable issue-management miniweb with a fixed action interface and fully observable business state; this round is not a real GitLab instance or WebArena.
local_experiment_guidance.shared_protocol: Same Luna model, observation/action permissions, trajectory data, task split, context and cumulative token/API budget for direct prediction, editable text-memory, and executable-code variants.
primary_evaluations: One-step prediction of independently observable business fields and page differences.
Open-loop 2-4-step prediction and closed-loop execution for unseen combinations of trained atomic actions.
Controlled action-precondition or side-effect change, time-to-repair and regression on unaffected rules.
fair_baselines: Luna direct predictor with same-history retrieval and editable non-executable text memory.
Luna-authored executable program with replay-based repair (main treatment).
No-model UI agent/script and privileged oracle upper bound.
local_experiment_guidance.reporting: Separate fixed-model unseen-state generalization from online update; report model prediction, task success, recovery, latency, LLM calls/tokens and model-maintenance cost separately.
local_experiment_guidance.reproduction_label: WMA, WebEvolver and VeriEnv depend on released/specified model weights and/or fine-tuning pipelines. Luna interface adaptation is a derived implementation, not reproduction of original trained results. Code/world-model approaches must likewise be labeled as local adaptations unless original model, data, environment and protocol are reproduced.
local_experiment_guidance.next_stage_environment: A fixed-version real GitLab deployment may be considered in a later UI/API speed-comparison stage after checking side-effect and permission equivalence; it is not the current experiment setting.
